newsitem.title: JAPAN: All Tokyo precious metals close higher.
newsitem.headline: All Tokyo precious metals close higher.

text.p: All Tokyo gold futures ended higher on Monday, reflecting the New York market's price gains overnight and the yen's falls against the dollar, traders said.
Yen-based gold futures ended seven to 10 yen higher, with the most active December up eight yen at 1,330 yen per gram. The day's volume was 41,980 lots.
Spot gold was quoted at $354.85/355.25 per ounce at 0730 GMT, against Friday's New York close of $355.30/355.80 and the Tokyo close on Friday at $354.40/354.90.
Local investors actively sold at distant months of the Tokyo futures, while trade houses rushed to buy, traders said.
Trade houses instead generated selling in the spot market, capping the topside of bullion prices, traders said.
"We're watching if the spot market can be supported at this level during European trading tonight," a trader said.
The New York market remains open on Monday, but the Martin Luther King Jr holiday in the United States may slow trade, New York traders said.
Yen-based platinum futures ended higher in all months, in line with gold. Prices were two to seven yen higher, with benchmark December finishing up two at 1,345 yen per gram.
Local traders said they were still waiting for notice from Moscow on annual negotiations on platinum group metal exports.
"What I can say is we're still waiting," another trade house official said. A Russian trade official in Tokyo said he had not received any formal notice from Moscow on the delayed negotiations yet.
Benchmark December silver futures were up 1.6 yen per 10 grams at 180.8 yen, and December palladium was up one yen at 456 yen.
